\section{Data Tables}
This table-heavy fixture exercises plain \texttt{tabular} environments so that
the tests can confirm tabular cell content is extracted as readable text. Each
table below carries its own distinctive, searchable sentinel string that
appears nowhere else in the document, alongside a shared ``Metric / Value``
header so that header-row extraction can be asserted across every table.

\subsection{Measurement Summary}
The first table records a small set of measurement sentinels. The marker
\texttt{tablesentinel-alpha} is the primary assertion target for this table.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|}
\hline
Metric & Value \\
\hline
alpha & tablesentinel-alpha \\
beta & 42 \\
gamma & 3.14159 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

A short paragraph of filler prose follows the first table so that the document
reads as genuine narrative rather than a bare sequence of tables. It repeats
the sentinel \texttt{tablesentinel-alpha} so that the assertion remains robust
whether or not the in-cell occurrence survives extraction intact.

\subsection{Component Inventory}
The second table lists a handful of components. It carries the distinctive
marker \texttt{tablesentinel-beta} in the first data cell.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|l|r|l|}
\hline
Component & Count & Status \\
\hline
tablesentinel-beta & 7 & active \\
widget & 3 & active \\
gadget & 12 & retired \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{Calibration Readings}
The third table reports a calibration reading table. Its distinctive marker is
\texttt{tablesentinel-gamma}, placed in the final data cell so that text near
the end of a row is captured as well as text near the start.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|r|l|}
\hline
Reading & Label \\
\hline
1 & low \\
2 & medium \\
3 & tablesentinel-gamma \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\newpage

\subsection{Longer Annotation}
This final subsection adds prose filler on the second page so that the fixture
spans at least two pages. It closes by reiterating the header phrase ``Metric
/ Value`` and the marker \texttt{tablesentinel-alpha} once more, ensuring the
section heading and at least one sentinel appear even if an entire early table
is lost during extraction. The three sentinels -- alpha, beta, and gamma --
remain the canonical targets for the automated tests in this stage.
